thread_analysis.thread_summary: Short internal report review thread (202 lines) for Koizumi Lighting Technology Corp. DIS profile test. Single issue: discrepancy between 4-digit PTS version in test log (8.10.2.3) and 3-digit version in report (8.10.2). Sakai confirmed 3-digit format is acceptable per SIG release management convention — the 4th digit can be omitted. Report approved with no changes required.
all_questions_found: Is a 3-digit PTS version (X.Y.Z) acceptable when the log shows 4 digits (X.Y.Z.W)?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: SIG uses 3-digit PTS version notation (X.Y.Z) in official release management. The 4th digit is a build sub-version that does not need to appear in qualification reports. Allion's standard template uses 3-digit format.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: 3-digit PTS version = acceptable. 4-digit also acceptable. Discrepancy between log (4-digit) and report (3-digit) is not flagged by SIG reviewers.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: None — this is purely a report formatting question with no real risk in either direction.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: No mistake — the engineer flagged it proactively for confirmation rather than assuming it was wrong.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Document in the report QC checklist that PTS versions in the 3-digit X.Y.Z format are always acceptable. Engineers should not spend time converting 3-digit to 4-digit or vice versa.
